title: Monday Teacher Plan
note: Expectations Wayground + grade check. No Blooket today. One turn-in per class: the exit ticket.

4th Period.topic: Strategy pattern, Day 1: find where things move
4th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can explain what a strategy is in one sentence and point to the 2 places in my game where a brick's strategy will go: my brick factory and update().
4th Period.exitTicket: What is a strategy, and in which function will your brick's strategy run every frame?
prep: Strategy Pattern assignment posted in Google Classroom with the Day 1 handout
Exit ticket question posted with both sentence frames
Your own Block Breaker Codespace open on the projector (game.js and bricks.js)

segments.title: Wayground: classroom expectations
segments.do: Students take the expectations Wayground.
segments.why: Monday routine: safety and predictability first (Maslow).
tips: Take attendance while they work.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the missed questions, then read the goal aloud: By the end of class, I can explain what a strategy is in one sentence and point to the 2 places in my game where a brick's strategy will go: my brick factory and update().
segments.why: Students know the target before work starts.
tips: Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: Grade check: Infinite Campus + form
segments.do: Students open Infinite Campus, find their overall grade, fill out the Weekly Grade Check-In form.
segments.why: Weekly ownership of grades.
tips: Keep grades private: no reading screens aloud.
Below 70%: point to the regrade form and Tuesday tutoring (3:15-4:00).
Exit tickets can't be redone; missing work is accepted late for full credit.

segments.title: This week and the points
segments.do: Walk the THIS WEEK box: Mon find, Tue plan, Wed trace, Thu build, Fri turn in once. 85 points for every box filled even if the game breaks, +15 if it works live.
segments.why: Points up front lowers the stakes (Maslow).
tips: Say it: only one turn-in, Friday.

segments.title: Mini-lesson: a strategy is a swappable behavior
segments.do: Map-app analogy: same Get directions button, swap car/walk/bike. Then the diagram: update() tells the BRICK to move; the brick holds stayStill or slide; SWAP.
segments.why: Concrete analogy before code (ELD: pre-teach STRATEGY, BRICK, SWAP).
tips: Turn-and-talk 1 minute: name another app where you swap a mode.
IS/NOT table: color is an attribute, moving is a behavior.

segments.title: I do: update() has no bricks
segments.do: Project game.js, Ctrl+F 'function update'. Read each line aloud: paddle moves, ball moves, bricks don't.
segments.why: Worked example from the real game (gradual release).
tips: Ask: which line moves the paddle? Cold call after think time.
Key idea: the empty spot is where the strategy will run.

segments.title: We do + You do: find update() and your brick factory
segments.do: Students open their own Codespace, find function update in game.js, then the line in their brick factory that builds each brick object. No code changes, no commit.
segments.why: Apply in their own code; small, guaranteed win.
tips: Ctrl+Shift+F searches all files.
If Copilot edits code: Ctrl+Z, don't accept.
Answer key: update() in game.js; makeBrick/makeBricks in bricks.js where list.push({ x, y, ... }) or return { ... } is.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom with a frame.
segments.why: One turn-in; recap the goal.
tips: Full answer: a strategy is a behavior you can swap; it will run in update() in game.js.
Accept 'a function you can swap' for the first part.

watchFor: Students editing code today: nothing should change.
Students who never found their brick factory last week: pair them with a neighbor.
Answers pasted from Copilot: remind 'your own words'.

6th Period.topic: Warren Truss Build, Day 1: side truss 1 (one strike)
6th Period.goal: By the end of class, my group has drawn our side truss full size with our measuring stick and built side truss 1 on top of it, every piece checked before gluing.
6th Period.exitTicket: What did your group build today, and how did you check a piece before gluing it?
prep: New table groups decided and posted (Seating-7th-2026-11)
Day 1 doc (7th_Mon_Side_Truss_1_Nov2) attached to the exit ticket (done)
Per table: 3 sheets of paper (measuring stick + drawing), tape, cardboard, glue, scissors
The 5 one-strike rules on the board
Truzme ready as the computer assignment for any group that loses materials

segments.title: Wayground: classroom expectations
segments.do: Students take the expectations Wayground.
segments.why: Monday routine: safety and predictability first (Maslow).
tips: Take attendance while they work.

segments.title: Review answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the missed questions, then read the goal aloud: By the end of class, I can name our 2 bridge rules and my group job, and I have drawn, supported and loaded one triangle in Truzme and saved it to my Google Drive.
segments.why: Students know the target before work starts.
tips: Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: Grade check: Infinite Campus + form
segments.do: Students open Infinite Campus, find their overall grade, fill out the Weekly Grade Check-In form.
segments.why: Weekly ownership of grades.
tips: Keep grades private: no reading screens aloud.
Below 70%: point to the regrade form and Tuesday tutoring (3:15-4:00).
Exit tickets can't be redone; missing work is accepted late for full credit.

segments.title: The one-strike materials rules
segments.do: Read the 5 rules from the doc's red box: nothing thrown, stay at your table, Chromebooks stay on the table, no touching others with materials, scissors stay on the table. One break by anyone = the whole group is on Chromebooks (Truzme) for the rest of the week. No warnings.
segments.why: Clear limits before materials come out, so the build stays a privilege they keep.
tips: Say it plainly: this is the build 6th did, and they're earning the materials back.
Students repeat the 5 rules chorally (ELD).

segments.title: New table groups + roles by birthday
segments.do: Move to new groups. Line up by birthday: youngest Builder, 2nd youngest Cutter, 2nd oldest Materials Manager, oldest Checker. Group of 3: Checker also MM. Group of 5: two Builders.
segments.why: Complex Instruction: roles with real authority; no one picks.
tips: Frontload the move: say where each group sits before anyone stands.
Checker also watches the 5 rules for the group.

segments.title: You do: fold the stick, draw, build side truss 1
segments.do: Fold a sheet the long way 3 times into a measuring stick (1 stick = 11 in; fold end to end for the ½ crease). Checker draws the plan full size on 2 taped sheets: bottom line 1½ sticks with a dot every ½ stick, 3 triangles, top line 1 stick. Then bottom chord, 6 diagonals, top chord: each traced along the stick, cut, checked and glued on the drawing. Press glue squares 30 s; shelf to dry.
segments.why: The same build 6th did; the drawing makes every piece checkable.
tips: Materials come out only after the rules are read and roles are set.
Walk the room the whole time. Call a strike at once, calmly, and move that group to Chromebooks.
A group on Chromebooks does the old Day 1 Truzme triangle (7th_Mon_Popsicle_Bridge_Plan_Day1_Nov2).
Sloppy folds: edges must line up before creasing, or every piece is off.

segments.title: Exit ticket
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom with a frame.
segments.why: One turn-in; recap the goal.
tips: Full answer: what they built plus how they checked it (with the stick, against the drawing).

watchFor: A group out of cardboard: bring it to their table; no one walks to the supply shelf.
Groups arguing about roles: point back to the birthday rule.
Side truss 1 must dry flat on the shelf for tomorrow.

7th Period.topic: Bridge Deck and Load Test, Day 1: join + deck
7th Period.goal: By the end of class, my group's two side trusses are joined 1/4 stick apart, and our bridge has a popsicle-stick deck with a stick on every bottom joint.
7th Period.exitTicket: Where did your group put the first 4 deck sticks, and why there?
prep: Before class: glue one popsicle stick to cardboard with a glue stick and tug-test it yourself
Bridge Deck and Load Test assignment posted with the Day 1 handout; exit ticket posted
Group bags, both side trusses, cut cross pieces, measuring sticks handed back
Popsicle sticks, glue sticks, scissors, scrap cardboard out

segments.do: Students take the expectations Wayground.

segments.title: This week and the points
segments.do: THIS WEEK box: Mon join + deck, Tue Test 1, Wed plan up to 6 tactical sticks, Thu add them, Fri Test 2 + turn in once.
segments.why: Predictable week (Maslow).

segments.title: Roles by birthday
segments.do: Youngest Joiner, 2nd youngest Deck Builder, 2nd oldest Materials Manager, oldest Checker. Group of 3: Checker also MM. Group of 5: two Deck Builders.
segments.why: Complex Instruction.

segments.title: I do: glue test + where the bottom joints are
segments.do: Show the side view: 4 bottom joints. Show the top view: first 4 deck sticks on the joints, then fill in. Key rule: weight goes on the joints.
segments.why: Structural reason before the build (Bloom: Understand to Apply).
tips: Ask: why on the joints? Think time, then a partner answer.

segments.title: You do: join sides + deck on the joints
segments.do: Glue test first, then stand sides 1/4 stick apart, glue 4 cross pieces, first 4 deck sticks on the joints, fill in (no gap wider than a glue square), count sticks, set to dry.
segments.why: Hands-on Apply with Checker approval on every piece.
tips: Publicly praise precise Checkers and Joiners (assign competence).
Deck sticks run ACROSS both bottom chords.
If glue sticks fail the tug test: switch to tape wraps or white glue if you have it.

segments.title: Exit ticket + set to dry
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom; bridges go flat to dry.
segments.why: One turn-in; recap the goal.
tips: Full answer: on the bottom joints, because that's where the diagonals/triangles meet and share the load.

watchFor: Sides glued too close or too far apart.
Deck sticks glued between joints first.
Glue sticks too weak for wood on cardboard.
Groups with only one side finished Friday: they finish side 2 first, deck tomorrow.

accommodations: Goal reviewed after the Wayground and again at the exit ticket; numbered steps; worked example first; checklists; two sentence frames on the exit ticket.
Key words with pictures (strategy/brick/swap; joint, deck, chord); choral repeat of the 2 bridge rules; partner talk before writing.
Lexend Deca; steps read aloud; speech-to-text OK; spelling not graded.
Short timed chunks with a visual timer; hands-on roles (Joiner, Checker); step-by-step pacing in Truzme; break pass.
Dictated exit tickets; extended time; floor: 8th finds update() only, 7th draws the triangle (save optional with help), 6th glues the 4 joint sticks only.
frameworks: Each grade starts the week's product: a moving brick, a bridge plan, a tested bridge.
Birthday-order roles with real authority in 6th and 7th; assign competence publicly.
Expectations, grade check, points up front, one turn-in, 'you are not behind'.
